description: Optional standout facts keyed by ISO3. Merged into country facts at load time with category "highlight".

highlights.AFG: Afghanistan's Band-e-Amir lakes are separated by natural mineral dams that the water built up over thousands of years.
highlights.AGO: Angola is the second-largest Portuguese-speaking country in the world by area, after Brazil.
highlights.ALB: Albania is dotted with more than 170,000 concrete bunkers built during the Cold War.
highlights.AND: Andorra is the only country in the world with Catalan as its sole official language.
highlights.ARE: The United Arab Emirates is home to the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building at over 828 meters.
highlights.ARG: Argentina has both the highest and the lowest points in the Southern Hemisphere—Mount Aconcagua and Laguna del Carbon.
highlights.ARM: Armenia was the first country in the world to adopt Christianity as its state religion, in the year 301.
highlights.ATG: Antigua is said to have a different beach for every day of the year—365 in all.
highlights.AUS: Australia is the only continent where all three groups of mammals—monotremes, marsupials, and placentals—live in the wild.
highlights.AUT: Austria's Schoenbrunn Zoo in Vienna opened in 1752 and is the oldest zoo in the world still operating.
highlights.AZE: Azerbaijan has more mud volcanoes than any other country—several hundred of them.
highlights.BDI: Burundi's eastern hills hold one of the most remote headwaters of the Nile, thousands of kilometers from the sea.
highlights.BEL: Belgium gave the world Tintin and the Smurfs, and comic strips are treated there as a serious art form.
highlights.BEN: Benin's village of Ganvie is built entirely on stilts in a lagoon, with markets held from canoes.
highlights.BFA: The name Burkina Faso means "land of upright people," chosen in 1984 to replace Upper Volta.
highlights.BGD: Bangladesh shares the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest on Earth and a stronghold for Bengal tigers.
highlights.BGR: Bulgaria's Valley of Roses supplies much of the world's rose oil, a key ingredient in perfume.
highlights.BHR: Bahrain's Tree of Life has survived alone in the desert for centuries with no obvious source of water.
highlights.BHS: The Bahamas is made up of roughly 700 islands, but only about 30 of them are inhabited.
highlights.BIH: Bosnia and Herzegovina has only about 20 kilometers of coastline, one of the shortest of any coastal country.
highlights.BLR: Belarus protects part of Europe's last primeval lowland forest, where wild European bison still roam.
highlights.BLZ: Belize is the only country in Central America where English is the official language.
highlights.BMU: Despite its Caribbean reputation, Bermuda sits alone in the North Atlantic, about 1,000 kilometers off North Carolina.
highlights.BOL: Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni is the world's largest salt flat and is so level that satellites use it for calibration.
highlights.BRA: Brazil contains about 60% of the Amazon rainforest—the largest tropical rainforest on Earth.
highlights.BRB: Barbados is built from coral limestone rather than volcanic rock, unlike most of its island neighbors.
highlights.BRN: Brunei's royal palace has nearly 1,800 rooms, making it one of the largest residences in the world.
highlights.BTN: Bhutan is one of the only countries in the world that absorbs more CO₂ than it emits.
highlights.BWA: Botswana's Okavango Delta is a river that never reaches the sea—it spreads out and evaporates in the Kalahari.
highlights.CAF: The Central African Republic sits almost exactly at the geographic center of the African continent.
highlights.CAN: Canada has more lakes than every other country in the world combined.
highlights.CHE: Switzerland has enough public and private shelters to house its entire population.
highlights.CHL: Chile's Atacama Desert is the driest place on Earth outside the poles, with spots that may go decades without rain.
highlights.CHN: Mandarin has more native speakers than any other language—most of them live in China.
highlights.CIV: Ivory Coast grows more cocoa than any other country—close to a third of the world's supply.
highlights.CMR: Cameroon is nicknamed "Africa in miniature" because it packs deserts, rainforests, mountains, and coast into one country.
highlights.COD: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has the world's deepest river—the Congo plunges more than 220 meters in places.
highlights.COG: The capital of the Republic of the Congo, Brazzaville, sits close enough to Kinshasa to see it across the river.
highlights.COK: The Cook Islands' 15 small islands are scattered across nearly two million square kilometers of ocean.
highlights.COL: Colombia has more bird species than any other country on Earth.
highlights.COM: Comoros is one of the world's leading producers of ylang-ylang, a flower used in famous perfumes.
highlights.CPV: Cape Verde's islands had no human inhabitants at all until sailors arrived in the 1460s.
highlights.CRI: Costa Rica has had no standing army since 1948 and runs on almost entirely renewable electricity.
highlights.CUB: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean and has more coastline than any other island in the region.
highlights.CYP: Cyprus's capital, Nicosia, is the last divided capital city in Europe.
highlights.CZE: Czechia has more castles and chateaux per square kilometer than any other country.
highlights.DEU: Long stretches of Germany's autobahn network have no general speed limit at all.
highlights.DJI: Djibouti's Lake Assal is the lowest point in Africa and one of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth.
highlights.DMA: Dominica's Boiling Lake is one of the largest hot springs in the world, and it genuinely bubbles.
highlights.DNK: Denmark's kingdom includes Greenland, the largest island in the world.
highlights.DOM: The Dominican Republic has the highest mountain in the Caribbean, Pico Duarte, at over 3,000 meters.
highlights.DZA: Algeria is the largest country in Africa, and more than four-fifths of it is Sahara desert.
highlights.ECU: The summit of Ecuador's Mount Chimborazo is the farthest point on the surface from the center of the Earth.
highlights.EGY: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and the only one still standing.
highlights.ERI: Eritrea's capital, Asmara, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its remarkably intact Art Deco architecture.
highlights.ESP: Spain produces roughly half the world's olive oil, more than any other country.
highlights.EST: Estonia was the first country in the world to hold nationwide elections with online voting.
highlights.ETH: Ethiopia's calendar has 13 months and runs about seven years behind the one used in most of the world.
highlights.FIN: Finland has around 188,000 lakes—more lakes per person than any other country.
highlights.FJI: Fiji is made up of more than 300 islands, and the 180th meridian runs straight through it.
highlights.FRA: France is the most visited country in the world, welcoming tens of millions more tourists than it has residents.
highlights.FSM: The Federated States of Micronesia contains Nan Madol, an ancient stone city built on nearly 100 artificial islets.
highlights.GAB: Almost 90% of Gabon is rainforest, and it set aside a tenth of its land as national parks all at once.
highlights.GBR: No place in the United Kingdom is more than about 125 kilometers from the sea.
highlights.GEO: Georgia's Caucasus mountains hold the deepest known cave on Earth, descending more than two kilometers.
highlights.GHA: Ghana's Lake Volta is the largest reservoir in the world by surface area.
highlights.GIN: Guinea is where the Niger River begins, before it loops nearly 4,200 kilometers through West Africa.
highlights.GMB: The Gambia is mainland Africa's smallest country, a narrow ribbon of land wrapped around a river.
highlights.GNB: Guinea-Bissau's Bijagos Archipelago has 88 islands, but only about 20 are permanently inhabited.
highlights.GNQ: Equatorial Guinea is the only African country with Spanish as an official language, and its capital sits on an island.
highlights.GRC: Greece has roughly 6,000 islands and islets, yet fewer than 230 of them are inhabited.
highlights.GRD: Grenada is nicknamed the Isle of Spice and grows a large share of the world's nutmeg.
highlights.GRL: Greenland's ice sheet holds about 8% of the world's fresh water and is more than 3 kilometers thick in places.
highlights.GTM: Guatemala's Lake Atitlan fills an ancient volcanic crater and is the deepest lake in Central America.
highlights.GUY: Guyana's Kaieteur Falls drops in a single plunge about five times the height of Niagara Falls.
highlights.HND: Honduras protects Rio Platano, one of the largest surviving rainforests north of the Amazon.
highlights.HRV: The necktie takes its name from Croatian soldiers, whose "cravat" style spread across Europe in the 1600s.
highlights.HTI: Haiti's Citadelle Laferriere is the largest fortress in the Americas, built on a mountaintop after independence.
highlights.HUN: Budapest sits above more than 100 thermal springs, more than any other capital city.
highlights.IDN: Indonesia is made up of more than 17,000 islands, spread across three time zones.
highlights.IND: India recognizes 22 official languages; hundreds more are spoken across the country.
highlights.IRL: Ireland has no native snakes—none ever made it across after the last ice age.
highlights.IRN: Iran's Lut Desert has recorded some of the hottest land surface temperatures ever measured on Earth.
highlights.IRQ: Iraq covers ancient Mesopotamia, where the world's earliest known writing and cities appeared.
highlights.ISL: Iceland has no native mosquito species—the cold climate keeps them from establishing populations.
highlights.ISR: More than half of Israel is desert, yet it recycles a larger share of its wastewater than any other country.
highlights.ITA: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country.
highlights.JAM: Jamaica is the only home of the giant swallowtail, the largest butterfly in the Western Hemisphere.
highlights.JOR: Jordan's ancient city of Petra was carved directly into sandstone cliffs and stayed hidden from outsiders for centuries.
highlights.JPN: Japan has one of the highest densities of vending machines in the world—roughly one for every 23 people.
highlights.KAZ: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world, bigger than all of Western Europe.
highlights.KEN: Kenya's Lake Turkana is the largest desert lake in the world.
highlights.KGZ: Kyrgyzstan's Lake Issyk-Kul is so deep and slightly salty that it never freezes, even in mountain winters.
highlights.KHM: Cambodia's Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument on Earth, and it appears on the national flag.
highlights.KIR: Kiribati is one of the few countries with territory in all four hemispheres.
highlights.KNA: St. Kitts and Nevis is the smallest country in the Americas by both area and population.
highlights.KOR: On South Korea's Jeju Island, generations of women called haenyeo have free-dived for seafood without oxygen tanks.
highlights.KWT: Kuwait has no rivers or natural lakes and gets most of its drinking water from the sea.
highlights.LAO: Laos is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia.
highlights.LBN: The cedar on Lebanon's flag is a real tree—some of its mountain cedars are more than 1,000 years old.
highlights.LBR: Liberia is one of only three countries in the world that has never officially adopted the metric system.
highlights.LBY: Libya built the Great Man-Made River, the world's largest irrigation project, to pipe ancient groundwater across the Sahara.
highlights.LCA: St. Lucia has produced more Nobel laureates per person than any other country.
highlights.LIE: Liechtenstein is one of only two doubly landlocked countries—you must cross two borders to reach the sea.
highlights.LKA: Sri Lanka's Sigiriya is an ancient royal palace built on top of a 200-meter rock column.
highlights.LSO: Lesotho is a true enclave—every border it has is with South Africa.
highlights.LTU: A monument north of Vilnius marks one geographers' calculation of the geographic center of Europe.
highlights.LUX: Luxembourg was the first country in the world to make all public transport free nationwide.
highlights.LVA: Latvia's Venta Rapid is the widest waterfall in Europe, even though it is only about two meters tall.
highlights.MAR: Morocco's University of al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859, is the oldest continuously operating university in the world.
highlights.MCO: Monaco is smaller in area than New York's Central Park.
highlights.MDA: Beneath Moldova's hills runs a maze of limestone tunnels stretching for more than 200 kilometers.
highlights.MDG: About 90% of the wildlife in Madagascar is found nowhere else on Earth.
highlights.MDV: Maldives is the world's flattest and lowest country, averaging only about 1.5 meters above sea level.
highlights.MEX: Mexico City is sinking several centimeters a year because it was built on a drained lake bed.
highlights.MHL: The Marshall Islands created the world's largest shark sanctuary, banning commercial shark fishing in all its waters.
highlights.MKD: North Macedonia shares Lake Ohrid, one of Europe's deepest lakes and among the oldest in the world.
highlights.MLI: Mali's city of Timbuktu held libraries with hundreds of thousands of handwritten manuscripts.
highlights.MLT: Malta's megalithic temples are older than the Egyptian pyramids and among the oldest free-standing buildings on Earth.
highlights.MMR: Myanmar's plain of Bagan holds more than 2,000 ancient temples and pagodas in a single valley.
highlights.MNE: Montenegro's Tara River carved the deepest canyon in Europe, plunging more than 1,300 meters.
highlights.MNG: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated fully sovereign country in the world.
highlights.MOZ: Mozambique has one of Africa's longest coastlines, running about 2,500 kilometers along the Indian Ocean.
highlights.MRT: Mauritania's Richat Structure is a giant bullseye in the Sahara, 40 kilometers wide and clearly visible from space.
highlights.MUS: Mauritius was the only place the dodo ever lived.
highlights.MWI: Lake Malawi has more species of fish than any other lake in the world.
highlights.MYS: Malaysia is home to the rafflesia, the world's largest single flower, which can grow a meter across.
highlights.NAM: Namibia's Namib is thought to be the oldest desert on Earth, arid for at least 55 million years.
highlights.NER: Niger's Tenere desert once held the loneliest tree on Earth, with no other tree within 400 kilometers.
highlights.NGA: Nigeria's film industry, Nollywood, releases more movies each year than Hollywood does.
highlights.NIC: Lake Nicaragua is the largest lake in Central America and is one of the few with sharks that swim in from the sea.
highlights.NIU: Niue is one of the world's largest raised coral atolls and the first entire country certified as a dark-sky place.
highlights.NLD: About a quarter of the Netherlands is below sea level, protected by an extensive system of dikes and pumps.
highlights.NOR: Norway has the world's longest road tunnel, running 24.5 kilometers straight through a mountain.
highlights.NPL: Nepal's flag is the world's only national flag that is not a quadrilateral.
highlights.NRU: Nauru is the world's smallest island country and has no official capital city.
highlights.NZL: New Zealand's only native land mammals are bats—every other mammal there was brought by people.
highlights.OMN: Oman's Dhofar region is one of the few places on Earth where frankincense trees grow wild.
highlights.PAK: Pakistan contains five of the world's fourteen peaks above 8,000 meters, including K2.
highlights.PAN: Because of the twist in Panama's isthmus, the sun can rise over the Pacific and set over the Atlantic.
highlights.PER: Peru grows more than 3,000 varieties of potato—the crop was first domesticated in its highlands.
highlights.PHL: The Philippines is made up of more than 7,600 islands, and thousands of them have no name.
highlights.PLW: Palau has a lake filled with millions of golden jellyfish that have lost almost all of their sting.
highlights.PNG: More than 800 languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea—more than in any other country.
highlights.POL: Poland's Wieliczka salt mine contains chapels, statues, and chandeliers carved entirely out of salt.
highlights.PRK: The Demilitarized Zone between North Korea and South Korea has become an accidental wildlife refuge.
highlights.PRT: Portugal supplies about half the world's cork, harvested from oak bark without cutting down the trees.
highlights.PRY: Paraguay generates almost all of its electricity from hydropower and exports much of it to its neighbors.
highlights.PSE: Palestine's city of Jericho lies more than 250 meters below sea level and is among the oldest settlements on Earth.
highlights.QAT: Qatar is so flat that its highest natural point is only about 100 meters above sea level.
highlights.ROU: Romania's Palace of the Parliament is the heaviest building in the world.
highlights.RUS: Russia spans eleven time zones—more than any other country.
highlights.RWA: Rwanda banned single-use plastic bags back in 2008, years ahead of most of the world.
highlights.SAU: Saudi Arabia has no permanent rivers; water comes from desalination, aquifers, and seasonal wadis.
highlights.SDN: Sudan has more ancient pyramids than Egypt—around 200 of them, built by the kingdom of Kush.
highlights.SEN: Senegal reaches the westernmost point of mainland Africa, and one of its lakes turns bright pink in the dry season.
highlights.SGP: Singapore banned most chewing-gum sales in 1992 to keep public spaces clean.
highlights.SLB: The Solomon Islands is made up of nearly 1,000 islands, where more than 70 languages are spoken.
highlights.SLE: Sierra Leone's capital, Freetown, sits on one of the largest natural harbors in the world.
highlights.SLV: El Salvador is the smallest country on the American mainland, and it has more than 20 volcanoes.
highlights.SMR: San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic, dating its founding to the year 301.
highlights.SOM: Somalia has the longest coastline of any country on mainland Africa.
highlights.SRB: Serbia is one of the world's largest exporters of raspberries.
highlights.SSD: South Sudan became the world's newest country in 2011 and contains the vast Sudd, one of Africa's biggest wetlands.
highlights.STP: Sao Tome and Principe straddles the equator, which crosses one of its tiny uninhabited islets.
highlights.SUR: Suriname is the most forested country on Earth—more than 90% of it is still rainforest.
highlights.SVK: Slovakia has more than 6,000 known caves beneath its mountains.
highlights.SVN: Slovenia's caves are home to the olm, a pale blind salamander once believed to be a baby dragon.
highlights.SWE: Sweden's "right of public access" lets anyone hike, forage, or camp on most land, even land they do not own.
highlights.SWZ: eSwatini changed its name from Swaziland in 2018, partly to stop the mix-up with Switzerland.
highlights.SYC: Seychelles is the only home of the coco de mer palm, which produces the largest seed of any plant.
highlights.SYR: Damascus, the capital of Syria, is one of the longest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
highlights.TCD: Chad's namesake lake has shrunk to a small fraction of its former size within living memory.
highlights.TGO: Togo is one of Africa's narrowest countries—barely 115 kilometers wide but stretching 550 kilometers inland.
highlights.THA: Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia never colonized by a European power.
highlights.TJK: More than nine-tenths of Tajikistan is mountainous, and about half the country lies above 3,000 meters.
highlights.TKM: Turkmenistan has a desert gas crater that has been burning continuously since the 1970s.
highlights.TLS: East Timor shares its island with Indonesia and became fully independent in 2002, one of Asia's youngest countries.
highlights.TON: Tonga sits just west of the date line, making it one of the first places on Earth to start each new day.
highlights.TTO: Trinidad and Tobago has Pitch Lake, the largest natural deposit of asphalt in the world.
highlights.TUN: Tunisia contains Cape Angela, the northernmost point of the entire African continent.
highlights.TUR: Turkey's largest city, Istanbul, is the only major city in the world that sits on two continents.
highlights.TUV: Tuvalu earns a large share of its national income from renting out its ".tv" internet domain.
highlights.TWN: Taiwan has more than 200 mountain peaks above 3,000 meters, despite being smaller than Switzerland.
highlights.TZA: Tanzania's Mount Kilimanjaro is the tallest free-standing mountain on Earth, rising straight out of the plains.
highlights.UGA: Uganda's forests shelter roughly half of all the mountain gorillas left in the world.
highlights.UKR: Ukraine sits on some of the world's most fertile black soil, which helped make it a leading grain exporter.
highlights.URY: Uruguay generates nearly all of its electricity from renewable sources, mostly wind and water.
highlights.USA: The United States has no official language at the federal level.
highlights.UZB: Uzbekistan borders the Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, which has almost entirely dried up.
highlights.VAT: Vatican City is the world's smallest independent state by both area and population.
highlights.VCT: St. Vincent and the Grenadines is a chain of 32 islands and cays, most of them uninhabited.
highlights.VEN: Venezuela's Angel Falls is the tallest waterfall in the world, dropping nearly a kilometer in one stretch.
highlights.VNM: Vietnam's Son Doong is the largest known cave passage on Earth—tall enough to fit a skyscraper inside.
highlights.VUT: Vanuatu's Mount Yasur has erupted almost nonstop for centuries, making it one of the most accessible active volcanoes.
highlights.WSM: Samoa skipped an entire day in 2011, jumping from Thursday to Saturday to switch sides of the date line.
highlights.XKX: Kosovo has the youngest population in Europe, with a median age under 30.
highlights.YEM: Yemen's island of Socotra has hundreds of plants found nowhere else, including the umbrella-shaped dragon's blood tree.
highlights.ZAF: South Africa has three capital cities—Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein.
highlights.ZMB: Zambia shares Victoria Falls, which forms the largest single sheet of falling water in the world.
highlights.ZWE: Zimbabwe is named after Great Zimbabwe, a vast stone city built without any mortar.
